articles.title: Tabletop Black Hole Glows, Proving Hawking Right
articles.summary: Physicists built a black hole analogue using light in an optical fiber and, for the first time, detected both Hawking radiation and its back reaction. The glow, at 233 nanometers, shifted the pump pulse's color, showing the black hole losing energy—just as Hawking predicted in 1974.

articles.title: From Ancient China to a $6,696 Scoop: Ice Cream's Wild History
articles.summary: National Ice Cream Month traces back to 1984, but ice cream's origins are ancient. Chinese Tang Dynasty emperors ate a frozen milk dessert, and a 2014 Wisconsin festival saw a 3,010-pound scoop carved by snow sculptors. Your flavor choice might even reveal your personality.

articles.title: Argentina: From Gauchos to Glaciers, a South American Giant
articles.summary: Argentina, the world's eighth-largest country, spans the Andes, the Pampas, and Patagonia. Its capital, Buenos Aires, is called the 'Paris of South America.' Iguazú Falls stretches 1.6 miles, and Cerro Aconcagua soars to 22,384 feet. Nearly half the population lives in the Buenos Aires area.
